paragraphs: Per Virginia Code Sec. 3.2-6200 Definitions. (Virginia Statutes (2016 Edition)), § 3.2-6200. Definitions.
As used in this chapter, unless the context requires a different meaning:

“Engages in an equine activity” means: (i) any person, whether mounted or unmounted, who rides, handles, trains, drives, assists in providing medical or therapeutic treatment of, or is a passenger upon an equine; (ii) any person who participates in an equine activity but does not necessarily ride, handle, train, drive, or ride as a passenger upon an equine; (iii) any person visiting, touring or utilizing an equine facility as part of an event or activity; or (iv) any person who assists a participant or equine activity sponsor or management in an equine activity. The term “engages in an equine activity” does not include being a spectator at an equine activity, except in cases where the spectator places himself in an unauthorized area and in immediate proximity to an equine or equine activity. ________ Initials
“Equine” means a horse, pony, mule, donkey, or hinny. ________ Initials

“Equine activity” means: (i) equine shows, fairs, competitions, performances, or parades that involve any or all breeds of equines and any of the equine disciplines, including dressage, hunter and jumper horse shows, grand prix jumping, three-day events, combined training, rodeos, driving, pulling, cutting, polo, steeple chasing, endurance trail riding and western games, and hunting; (ii) equine training or teaching activities; (iii) boarding equines; (iv) riding, inspecting, or evaluating an equine belonging to another whether or not the owner has received some monetary consideration or other thing of value for the use of the equine or is permitting a prospective purchaser of the equine to ride, inspect, or evaluate the equine; (v) rides, trips, hunts, or other equine activities of any type however informal or impromptu that are sponsored by an equine activity sponsor; (vi) conducting general hoof care, including placing or replacing horseshoes or hoof trimming of an equine; and (vii) providing or assisting in breeding or therapeutic veterinary treatment. ________ Initials

“Equine activity sponsor” means any person or his agent who, for profit or not for profit, sponsors, organizes, or provides the facilities for an equine activity, including pony clubs, 4-H clubs, hunt clubs, riding clubs, school- and college-sponsored classes and programs, therapeutic riding programs, and operators, instructors, and promoters of equine facilities, including stables, clubhouses, pony-ride strings, fairs, and arenas where the activity is held. ________ Initials

“Equine professional” means a person or his/her agent engaged for compensation in: (i) instructing a participant or renting to a participant an equine for the purpose of riding, driving, or being a passenger upon an equine; or (ii) renting equipment or tack to a participant. ________ Initials

“Intrinsic dangers of equine activities” means those dangers or conditions that are an integral part of equine activities, including: (i) the propensity of equines to behave in ways that may result in injury, harm, or death to persons on or around them; (ii) the unpredictability of an equine’s reaction to such things as sounds, sudden movement, and unfamiliar objects, persons, or other animals; (iii) certain hazards such as surface and subsurface conditions; (iv) collisions with other animals or objects; and (v) the potential of a participant acting in a negligent manner that may contribute to injury to the participant or others, such as failing to maintain control over the equine or not acting within the participant’s ability. ________ Initials
“Participant” means any person, whether amateur or professional, who engages in an equine activity, whether or not a fee is paid to participate in the equine activity. ________ Initials
1991, c. 358, § 3.1-796.130; 2003, c. 876; 2008, c. 860; Virginia Code Sec. 3.2-6201 Horse racing excluded. (Virginia Statutes (2016 Edition))     § 3.2-6201. Horse racing excluded.
The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to horse racing, as that term is defined by § 59.1-365. 1991, c. 358, § 3.1-796.131; 2008, c. 860.
Virginia Code Sec. 3.2-6202 Liability limited; liability actions prohibited. (Virginia Statutes (2016 Edition))

A. Except as provided in § 3.2-6203, an equine activity sponsor, an equine professional, or any other person, which shall include a corporation, partnership, or limited liability company, shall not be liable for an injury to or death of a participant resulting from the intrinsic dangers of equine activities and, except as provided in § 3.2-6203, no participant nor any participant’s parent, guardian, or representative shall have or make any claim against or recover from any equine activity sponsor, equine professional, or any other person for injury, loss, damage, or death of the participant resulting from any of the intrinsic dangers of equine activities. ________ Initials

B. Except as provided in § 3.2-6203, no participant or parent or guardian of a participant who has knowingly executed a waiver of his rights to sue or agrees to assume all risks specifically enumerated under this subsection may maintain an action against or recover from an equine activity sponsor or an equine professional for an injury to or the death of a participant engaged in an equine activity. The waiver shall give notice to the participant of the intrinsic dangers of equine activities. The waiver shall remain valid indefinitely unless expressly revoked within fifteen (15) days in writing by the participant or parent or guardian of a minor. ________ Initials   1991, c. 358, § 3.1-796.132; 2003, c. 876; 2008, c. 860.

paragraphs: Thank you for your interest in donating your horse to Eagle’s Nest Veterans’ Equine Therapy (ENVET) program (501c3, EIN #88-0998372).  It is our mission to provide Veterans with free access to Horse Heroes, in order to help their recovery and daily activities.  The benefit of equine relationships with Veterans has been proven to help both the person and the horse.  The horses receive the love and attention of the Veterans, and the Veterans learn to build connections and communication, thereby bridging the gap between experience and emotion.
Due to the physical and demanding nature of our services, each Equine Candidate must be able to perform within certain standards, for the safety of our Veterans and our Hors Heroes, they must:
- be up to date on vaccinations, deworming, dental (teeth floated) and hoof/farrier care, and have a current Coggins (less than 30 Days old).
- be able to Walk/Trot/Canter in balanced gaits, and have no defects of the legs or spine, and be “sound” with or without a saddle and mounted rider; obedient to the rider’s voice and leg cues.
- not require special or corrective shoeing, be calm for the Farrier, and not need sedation to clean or trim feet.
- not require regular medications, expensive supplements, or injections to function on a daily basis.
- not have bad ground manners, vices, habits, or behaviors (aggressive or flighty), and must be even-tempered.
- not be over the age of 25 years, or under 5 years (special circumstances are considered).

Please fill out the equine’s information, in order to assist in the determination of whether your horse is a good Candidate for our Veteran program.  Pictures are helpful in positively identifying each horse, as many horses may have similar markings or coloring.  Registration papers are also helpful in making sure the horses are legitimately owned, and to transfer ownership to ENVET.  We do NOT surrender horses to slaughter.

If the Horse Candidate is suitable for our Veterans, we may accept the horse on a 60 to 90 day trial period.  Current (less than 30 day) dated and signed Veterinarian Letter, stating that the candidate horse is in acceptable health and has no lameness issues, is required.  The Horse Candidate may be accepted to our farm at any time during the trial period.  Occasionally, the trial period may be extended to allow further assessment, particularly if there are weather or scheduling issues, or circumstances and timing have not allowed for ample real-application experience.  Once the Horse Candidate is found to meet the criteria, the Donor will receive a Letter of Acceptance to sign, in order to officially transfer ownership and a Tax-Deductible Receipt.  During the trial period, the registered owner is responsible for feed, veterinary, and farrier costs.  Horse Candidates who do not pass the trial evaluation will be returned to the registered owner, as a right of first refusal.  Those owners who do not wish to have the horse returned to them will so state in the document below, and a suitable (no kill) rescue or alternate home will be considered; whichever is best for the happiness and health of the horse.

If accepted, the Candidate Horse will become part of the Therapy Team for the Veterans; as such, we strive to provide a happy and healthy home for the Horse Heroes.  Our Veterinarian of Record is Total Equine Veterinary Associates (TEVA), https://www.totalequinevets.com, 703.505.2320 , to whom all Equine Medical and Dental records shall be provided by the current veterinarian or veterinary professional.  Our Farrier of Record is Mr. Joe Wolfe, who may be reached through ENVET, to whom any/all farrier records or contacts should be provided.

We appreciate your consideration for our Veterans.  Candidate Horses welcome visitors they know, please come to visit!  Our Horse Heroes love to see their beloved Humans, as do we!  ENVET encourages visitation and Volunteerism from those who have provided mounts to this unique program.  We also welcome any donations to assist in defraying continuing costs for feed, hay, medical or dental care, and farrier visits.
